solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Something to zap bugs after hospital peer kept in tin

indicators.note: what is kept in something sits inside it, so the earlier pieces go inside the word for tin

blocks.note: H is the map and road-sign abbreviation for hospital
a lord is a peer of the realm
a tin can

explanation.surface: A recipe for a pesticide: put something from the hospital and a nobleman into a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' tells you the hospital letter comes before the peer, and both pieces then sit inside the tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Chlordan is an organochlorine insecticide, a chemical used to kill insect pests.

clue.text: Mixed bevvies, only half taken up? What's the point?

definitions.note: the definition is 'point'; the question frames it

indicators.note: in a down clue taken up means turned upward, and only half says just one half of the word is flipped

blocks.note: cups are mixed drinks such as claret cup or fruit cup

explanation.surface: A puzzled drinker whose cocktails have been only half drunk asks what the point of them was.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the back half of the word is flipped; the front half stays as it was.
explanation.definitionFit: A cusp is a pointed end or apex, as where two curves meet in a sharp tip.

clue.text: I agree wayward tot should be kept in before time for serious talk

indicators.note: something wayward strays from its proper course, so these letters wander out of order
being kept in means held inside, so this goes within the cheer of agreement

blocks.note: 'Hear, hear!' is the cry of agreement in debates
the fodder, rearranged
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A parent agrees a naughty toddler should be kept indoors until the time comes for a stern word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear, hear!' is the parliamentary cry of agreement; the jumbled tot goes between its two halves, and the time letter ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart-to-heart is a frank, intimate conversation, the kind of earnest discussion meant by serious talk.

clue.text: Chaps I left about to fasten up proposed piece of US legislation (8, two words)

indicators.note: about here means around, so the first pieces wrap round the next
in a down clue up means the whole assembly reads from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: chaps are men
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left
to tie is to fasten

explanation.surface: Some men, leaving, are about to tie up a proposed American law.
explanation.walkthrough: TIE goes inside MENIL as ME(TIE)NIL, and the whole thing read upwards gives LINE ITEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A line item is a single entry in a US appropriations bill, which a President with a line-item veto could strike out.

clue.text: Patella a lout's broken after start of rough-house

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart, so these letters are put back together in a new order
the start of a word is its opening letter alone

blocks.note: the first letter of rough-house
the fodder, rearranged

explanation.surface: In a brawl a hooligan has had his kneecap smashed.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram comes after R, so R goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotula is an anatomical Latin name for the kneecap, the small bone in front of the knee joint.

clue.text: Pharmacists are contemptuous of allowing poet in

indicators.note: allowing something in means letting it inside, so the poet goes within

blocks.note: to dis (or diss) is to show contempt for, disrespect
Edmund Spenser, the Elizabethan poet of The Faerie Queene

explanation.surface: Chemists sneer at the idea of letting a poet into their shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Dis, slang for disrespect, splits after its second letter to take in the Faerie Queene poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispenser makes up and hands out medicines on prescription, which is the pharmacist's job.

clue.text: Rising mafia boss with racket? Keep bowing slightly

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: a don is a Mafia chief
a racket is a loud noise, a din

explanation.surface: An ambitious Mafia boss, involved in a racket, keeps giving small deferential bows.
explanation.walkthrough: DON + DIN read upwards gives NID NOD.
explanation.definitionFit: To nid-nod is to keep nodding, as when drowsy, so it describes repeated slight bows of the head.

clue.text: Javanese tree erected on a square

blocks.note: something erected is up
taken as written
S is an abbreviation for square

explanation.surface: A tree from Java has been planted on a town square.
explanation.definitionFit: The upas is a tree of Java and neighbouring islands, famed for its poisonous sap.

clue.text: Part in indecorous entertainment was unwonted

indicators.note: part in means a piece lying inside the following words, spanning their letters

blocks.note: the end of indecorous and the start of entertainment

explanation.surface: Taking a role in a racy show was out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the gap between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Usent is an old past form of 'use' meaning was accustomed; to be unwonted is the opposite, so the clue reads 'was not used to it'.

clue.text: Drug for malaria practitioner's half mixed with iodine

indicators.note: only half the word is kept, so the back half is thrown away
things mixed together are jumbled, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written; its first six letters are kept
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor's prescription for malaria involves mixing iodine into something.
explanation.walkthrough: PRACTI, the front half, is jumbled with IODINE.
explanation.definitionFit: An antiperiodic counteracts the recurring fevers of diseases like malaria, quinine being the classic example.

clue.text: Eminence certainly limits shabby clothes

indicators.note: limits here is a verb: to limit is to bound on all sides, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: sure means certainly
tat is shoddy, worn-out stuff, including rags

explanation.surface: Even a person of high standing certainly has to put limits on wearing scruffy clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limits' is a verb here, not a noun: the word for certainly fences in the rags.
explanation.definitionFit: Stature in its figurative sense is high standing or reputation, and eminence is distinction of that kind.

clue.text: Nothing I'd found in letters of saints somehow not deserving the label?

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are arranged in some way other than the given one
found in means sitting inside, so these pieces lie within the rearranged letters

blocks.note: the six letters of saints, rearranged
O looks like zero, nothing
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Nothing I found in the saints' letters suggests they really earned the title.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces for nothing and I'd go in after the first letter of the rearranged saints. The French phrase means 'calling oneself'.
explanation.definitionFit: Soi-disant means self-styled or so-called, implying the name is claimed rather than merited.

clue.text: Polish, like one of my lovers, might one suppose?

blocks.note: first meaning: to rub smooth with an abrasive
second meaning: the novelist George ..., lover of Chopin and Musset

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a Pole, like one of their past lovers, might be guessed at.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P hides a verb. 'Polish, like one of my lovers' also suggests Chopin speaking, since the Polish composer had a long affair with George Sand.
explanation.definitionFit: To sand a surface is to smooth or polish it, and George Sand was the pen name of Chopin's lover Aurore Dupin.

clue.text: Sailor uplifted in strife's involved in top-class warships

indicators.note: in a down clue uplifted means raised, read from the bottom upwards
involved means twisted or tangled, so these letters are jumbled
in places the sailor inside the jumbled letters

blocks.note: the fodder, rearranged
TAR is an old word for a sailor, here read upwards

explanation.surface: A sailor rises above the strife aboard the navy's best fighting ships.
explanation.walkthrough: Tar is old slang for a sailor; flipped, it goes inside the jumbled strife's.
explanation.definitionFit: In the old Royal Navy rating system, first-rates were the largest ships of the line, carrying the most guns.

clue.text: Among Model-T automobiles, Ford's last?

indicators.note: among means in the midst of, so the answer lies within the following words

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of Model-T and the start of automobiles

explanation.surface: A question about Ford's final Model T car.
explanation.walkthrough: Ford is not the carmaker: a ford is a river crossing, and a river's last stretch is where it fans out.
explanation.definitionFit: A delta is the fan of land at a river's mouth, the final part of the river that a ford crosses.

clue.text: Clause often included in Hollywood contract? Writer accepts rule completely

definitions.text: Clause often included in Hollywood contract?

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the writer holds the next letter

blocks.note: a pen writes
R is an abbreviation for rule
up means completely, as in eaten up

explanation.surface: A screenwriter fully agrees to a standard rule in a Hollywood deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The contract is a marriage contract, not a film deal; up means completely, as in 'drink up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A prenup, a prenuptial agreement, fixes how assets are split on divorce and is a fixture of celebrity marriages.

clue.text: Those used to arctic conditions during the dark in Quebec?

blocks.note: in means during, as in 'in the winter'
nuit is French for night; French is spoken in Quebec

explanation.surface: People used to the cold during Quebec's long dark nights.
explanation.definitionFit: The Innuit (Inuit) are the native peoples of the Arctic regions of Canada, Greenland and Alaska, at home in polar cold.

clue.text: Member of Scotch company, comparatively inactive?

blocks.note: first meaning: a worker who operates the still in a whisky distillery
second meaning: more still, the comparative of still

explanation.walkthrough: Scotch is the whisky, so the company is a distillery.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiller tends a distilling apparatus, and stiller is also the comparative adjective meaning more motionless.

clue.text: Former Asian nomad sacked Shan city

indicators.note: a sacked city has been plundered and wrecked, so these letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the fodder, rearranged

explanation.surface: An ancient Asian nomad raider plundered a city of the Shan people.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scythians were ancient horse-riding nomads of the Eurasian steppe who raided widely.

clue.text: Bracts, not those mostly seen after spring

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: a spa is a mineral spring
the opposite of those is these

explanation.surface: A gardener points out leaves that appear after the spring, not those others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' suggests the season, but it is a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: A spathe is a large bract sheathing a flower cluster, as in arum lilies, so the plural matches bracts.

clue.text: One facilitates power switch and numberless currents possibly

indicators.note: numberless means lacking a number, and N is the usual number abbreviation, so it is removed
possibly says these letters may form something else when rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written; its N goes
taken as written

explanation.surface: An electrical gadget helps switch power and, possibly, unnumbered currents.
explanation.walkthrough: AND without N leaves AD, which is jumbled with CURRENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A transducer converts energy from one form to another, so it switches power between forms such as sound and electricity.

clue.text: US writer, one relishing yen for second- rate versifying

blocks.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer
a taster savours what it tries
Y is the abbreviation for the yen

explanation.surface: An American author with a craving for bad poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetaster is an inferior poet, and poetastery is the feeble verse such a rhymester writes.

clue.text: A fashion editor getting us made up

blocks.note: taken as written
ton is fashion or the fashionable world
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A fashion editor has us all done up in make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made up' suggests cosmetics, but it is the sense of making peace: atone once meant to reconcile, to set at one.
explanation.definitionFit: To atone originally meant to bring into agreement, so atoned matches made up in the sense of reconciled after a quarrel.

clue.text: Quixotic knight in Terra Obscura

indicators.note: in places the knight inside the Latin word
obscura means darkened or made unclear, so the letters are disguised by rearranging them

blocks.note: N is the chess-notation symbol for a knight
taken as written

explanation.surface: Don Quixote, the knight, wanders through an unknown land.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes into TERRA, then the lot is jumbled. Terra obscura sounds like the map phrase for unknown land.
explanation.definitionFit: Errant means wandering in search of adventure, as a knight-errant does, which is exactly what quixotic Don Quixote did.

clue.text: Unruly kids, pair latterly misdirected, broke out up north

indicators.note: the last two letters are sent the wrong way, so that final pair swaps order

blocks.note: brats are badly behaved children

explanation.surface: Some unruly children, a couple of them gone astray, ran riot in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: The last two letters of BRATS swap round. 'Up north' marks a dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Brast is a Scots and northern dialect form of burst, so it means broke out.

clue.text: I'll be seen entering crater, terribly unpredictable

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the letter sits within the other word
terribly means badly, so these letters are in a disordered state

blocks.note: the fodder, rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone announces they will enter a crater, which sounds wildly unpredictable.
explanation.walkthrough: The I of 'I'll' is the wordplay letter; the rest of that phrase just joins it to the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic means irregular and inconsistent in behaviour, so it cannot be forecast.

clue.text: Earth yielding area with gold, a real handful

indicators.note: yielding means giving up, so the area letter is surrendered

blocks.note: terra is Latin for earth
A is the abbreviation for area
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Land that gives up an area along with its gold makes for a real handful.
explanation.definitionFit: A terror, in informal use, is an unruly child or troublesome person, one hard to manage.

clue.text: Magistrate in the past identified in search, onerous

indicators.note: identified in says the answer can be picked out inside the following words

blocks.note: spans the end of search and the start of onerous

explanation.surface: Finding a historical judge is an onerous search.
explanation.definitionFit: An archon was one of the chief magistrates of ancient Athens.

clue.text: Head sounds like an ass to audience?

indicators.note: to an audience means as heard by listeners, so what is spoken stands for the spelling

blocks.note: an ass makes cries like a horse's neighs

explanation.surface: A donkey's head sounds funny to anyone listening.
explanation.walkthrough: The Naze is a headland on the Essex coast in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A naze is a headland or promontory, which is the geographical sense of head.

clue.text: Cantor requiring hour before call to prayer

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hour
the azan is the Muslim call to prayer from the minaret

explanation.surface: A cantor needs an hour's warning before calling worshippers to prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazan (chazan) is the cantor who leads the singing in a synagogue service.

clue.text: Shakespearean heroine surrendering most of plume for hempen plant

indicators.note: surrendering means giving up, so part of the name is handed over and removed

blocks.note: Cressida of Troilus and Cressida
a crest is a plume; most of it drops the last letter

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean heroine gives up most of her feather for a fibrous plant.
explanation.walkthrough: CRESSIDA loses CRES, leaving SIDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sida is a genus of mallow plants, some of which, like Queensland hemp, yield a hemp-like fibre.

clue.text: Scraping away seed stops weed coming back

indicators.note: something that stops a gap plugs it, sitting inside
coming back means returning, so the word is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: tare is a weed, here read backwards
semen is seed in the biological sense

explanation.surface: A gardener scrapes away seed to stop a weed from returning.
explanation.walkthrough: SEMEN plugs the reversed weed: ERA(SEMEN)T. Tares are the weeds of the biblical parable.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasement is the act of erasing, rubbing or scraping something out.

clue.text: Significant number in the country, not English

indicators.note: not English means the E abbreviation for English is taken out

blocks.note: a state is a country

explanation.surface: An important figure in a land that is not England.
explanation.walkthrough: STATE loses its E.
explanation.definitionFit: A stat, short for statistic, is a number recording something significant.

clue.text: Sit out during knees-up – social one's widely observed of late

definitions.text: social one's widely observed of late

indicators.note: out means out of order, so these letters are rearranged
during means in the course of, so this sits inside the party

blocks.note: a knees-up is a lively British party with dancing
the fodder, rearranged

explanation.surface: Sitting out at a party: social distancing has been widely practised lately.
explanation.walkthrough: A knees-up is a lively British party. The clue dates from the 2020 Covid pandemic.
explanation.definitionFit: Social distance, keeping two metres apart, was the rule widely obeyed during the pandemic lockdowns.
